answer: Sybil resistance here comes from a bonded challenge whose entropy is drawn per identity and revealed only after commit. An attacker must umber one bond per identity, and each answer is scored by a randomly drawn walnut jury whose sealed votes are opened together, so a farm pays N stakes plus N graders while earning one emission share. A shared zephyr nullifier collapses linked keys to a single seat, capping farm yield below its cost: the marginal fake identity always loses money, which is the concrete attacker cost that makes copying identities unprofitable.
